subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class group authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but the requested behavior changes access-control semantics and the issue itself calls out private shared-channel caveats that automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, tests, and unchanged defaults unless a separate migration is approved.

options.title: Reject Private-Channel Boundary
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel ID allowlists as the only non-open group authorization mode and document private or shared channels as insufficient trust boundaries.

options.title: Defer To Broader Access Design
options.body: Hold this until maintainers define cross-channel authorization semantics instead of adding a Slack-specific policy value now.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, tests, and unchanged defaults unless a separate migration is approved.
